title: Multiplying Fractions by Whole Numbers Worksheets
intro: Show multiplication by a whole number as repeated copies of a fraction.
html:
Teaching notes for parents and teachers

How to teach it

Use matching fraction strips to make the required number of copies. Count the pieces and discuss an equivalent simplified answer.

Example to work through together

Use the model below as you explain the example. Have your student point to the quantities as you discuss them.

Show three groups of three fourths. Each strip below represents a whole of the same size. Every whole has four equal parts, and three parts in each strip are shaded.

Count the shaded fourths: 3 + 3 + 3 = 9 fourths. Each piece is still one fourth of a whole. The product is 3/4 × 3 = 9/4 = 2 1/4, not 9/12. Eight fourths make two wholes, with one fourth left.

Ask your student

How many pieces of this size do all the copies contain?

If your student needs help

If the student multiplies the denominator by the whole number, point out that the piece size has not changed.
